persona.summary: The same homeowner and lien, entering through the civil (Superior Court) form.
persona.story: i hired a contractor to do interlock for my whole property, driveway, backyard and walkways, a big job, about 300000. he didnt finish the job and most of what he did was done bad, the base is bad and the slopes are wrong on all of the interlock. he also did extras i never agreed to in writing and charged me for them. i didnt pay the amount he wanted because i wanted the job finished properly first. when i told him on august 22 i didnt want him doing any more work he put a lien on my house on september 9 for 60000. the whole job was 300000

fields.Amount claimed or disputed: $60,000 lien on a $300,000 job; fixing the work will cost more
fields.Timeline: june 2026 hired, august 22 2026 told him to stop, september 9 2026 lien registered
fields.Evidence you have: signed quote, deposit receipt, his invoices, texts, photos, repair estimate

expect: The user is the HOMEOWNER whose house has a $60,000 construction lien registered on September 9, 2026 on a $300,000 job; he told the contractor to stop on August 22, 2026. Nothing has been filed by either side as far as he knows.

The lien must be recognised: it is enforced in the Superior Court of Justice; the contractor's time limits to preserve and perfect the lien, and the ways an owner can get a lien off title (paying money or security into court, a motion to discharge or declare it expired), should be pointed out with dates where the rules allow.
His own claim for the cost of fixing and finishing the work should be presented as an option with its court and form, not a recommendation.
The site must not say whether the lien is valid or who will win.
